text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The cabinet members listen to President Hrawi's remarks on the internal and regional situation at the first meeting of the government to discuss its policy statement.
-A United Nations programme informs Lebanon of its willingness to help in the toxic waste problem in the country.
-Hizbollah chief Sheikh Nasrallah urges MPs not to give a vote of confidence to the new government of Prime Minister Hariri.
-President Hrawi says the government's priorities should be the living conditions and administrative reform.
-Minister for displaced people Jumblatt continues his verbal campaign against Hariri, saying his new government is is tatters.
-Prime Minister Hariri tells a regional conference in Beirut: "Lebanon is at the threshold of a new start".
-Acting Finance Minister Siniora says the new accounting system will be implemented in Lebanon at the start of 1997.
-Israel issues new threats against Lebanon saying its forces can pursue Hizbollah guerrillas in every place and using all means.
-The posts and communications ministry received $50 million from cellular telephone revenue in Lebanon in the last 19 months.
-Israeli forces have detained a Lebanese man more than a month ago and taken him secretly to Israel.
-Central Bank Governor Salameh issues circular note to commercial banks and financial institutions organising special account transfer operations with the central bank.
-German mediator Schmidbauer returned to Israel in total secrecy in a bid to find a comprehensive solution to the issue of Arabs imprisoned by Israel and Israeli servicemen missing in Lebanon.
